reproduction_target: Multi-omic 3D epigenome roadmap of nine human B-cell differentiation stages: CUT&RUN / ATAC-seq / RNA-seq / liCHi-C primary processing (bowtie2, sambamba, samtools, deepTools, ChromTime, MACS3-HMMRATAC, Trim Galore, STAR, subread featureCounts, HiCUP, CHiCAGO), chromatin-state segmentation (ChromHMM), super-enhancer calling (ROSE), enhancer-gene assignment and network analysis (HiCaptuRe, igraph, pheatmap), TF footprinting (HOCOMOCO v13 + TOBIAS), enhancer-activity regulatory modelling (BIC model selection), bootstrap of primed loops, IHEC EpiAtlas chromatin-state reanalysis, dbGaP/St. Jude structural-variant and enhancer-deletion analyses (DESeq2, poolr), survival analysis, GO/pathway enrichment, and Gviz browser visualisation. Wet-lab work (tonsil/bone-marrow cell isolation and FACS sorting, CUT&RUN, ATAC-seq, RNA-seq and liCHi-C library construction, library QC, sequencing) is out of computational-reproduction scope.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis-invocation extracted from the 'Primary Data Processing Pipelines' through 'Epigenome Browser Data Visualization' Methods prose of the bioRxiv full text (JATS XML returned HTTP 403; the .full HTML landing/full-text page was used instead, HTTP 200). ATAC-seq primary processing is stated as 'processed as described for CUT&RUN' plus an offset-correction step and is therefore recorded as its own step rather than duplicating the CUT&RUN alignment/filter steps. Custom / in-house / unnamed-tool analyses (QC metrics script, consensus-peak merging, disjoin segmentation integration, enhancer specificity definition, TF-enrichment linear model, regulatory modelling, bootstrap, IHEC bin map, Gviz script) are each counted as one step because the Methods describe them as distinct analysis invocations. Repo landing page was read (README prose + top-level directory listing only); no workflow source was opened. Wet-lab procedures counted in W, not verdicted. Wet-lab steps are counted in W (7) but are not enumerated in the steps array, consistent with prior stage-1 reports: FACS isolation of nine populations, CUT&RUN, ATAC-seq, RNA-seq and liCHi-C library preparation, TapeStation library QC, and sequencing.

steps.label: CUT&RUN read trimming ('After trimming, reads were mapped...') - trimming tool and version not named for CUT&RUN
CUT&RUN alignment with bowtie2 (2.3.2) to GRCh38.p13, flags --very-sensitive-local --no-unal --no-mixed --no-discordant -k 2 --phred33 -I 10 -X 700 --dovetail
CUT&RUN filtering with sambamba (0.7.0) and deduplication with samtools (1.9)
BigWig generation with deepTools (3.2.1) bamCoverage (CUT&RUN and ATAC-seq)

Histone-mark peak calling (H3K27ac, H3K4me3) with ChromTime (v1.0.0) across 8 stages / 2 trajectories; q-value 0.01, q-value-seed 0.01, p-value-extend 0.01, otherwise default; BAM->BED conversion, replicate averaging, trajectory intersection
ATAC-seq primary processing 'as described for CUT&RUN' plus paired-read offset correction (offset tool/parameters not specified)
ATAC-seq peak calling with HMMRATAC as implemented in MACS3 v3.0.2, default settings
Consensus ATAC peak set per cell type: merge all peaks, keep those supported (partially or totally) by >=2 replicates (no tool named)
RNA-seq adapter trimming with Trim Galore (0.6.6), ENCODE standards
RNA-seq alignment with STAR (2.7.0f) to GRCh38.p13 using 'parameters recommended by ENCODE' (multi-mapper filtering, overhang/mismatch tuning; exact flags not listed)
Read quantification with featureCounts from subread (2.0.2), arguments -O and --countReadPairs
liCHi-C read processing with HiCUP (0.8.2): in-silico digest, mapping to GRCh38.p13, artifact filtering, deduplication, capture-efficiency filtering to unique captured valid reads
Promoter-interaction calling with CHiCAGO R package (1.14.0) on merged samples; high-confidence interactions defined as CHiCAGO score >= 5

Clustering of promoter interactions: k-means on asinh-transformed CHiCAGO scores + per-cluster specificity score; hierarchical clustering (average linkage, Euclidean) and PCA with R prcomp (no R or package versions, k not stated)
Interaction data handling / virtual-4C generation with the HiCaptuRe Bioconductor R package (no version given)
Library-complexity QC metrics NRF / PBC1 / PBC2 computed with an 'in-house script' (ENCODE-recommended metrics; thresholds not numerically stated)
Fragment-size distribution from BAM via samtools-based scripts and signal-to-noise (AUC) via deepTools fingerprintPlot

Chromatin-state segmentation with ChromHMM (v1.24): BinarizeBam (broad PTMs) / BinarizeBed (narrow PTMs from ChromTime peaks), 15-state LearnModel trained on B-cell types, MakeSegmentation + MakeBrowserFiles applied to control cell types
Manual biological relabelling of the 15 emission states + integration of segmentations with ATAC peaks via a 'disjoin approach' (no tool, no version, no rule table)

Super-enhancer identification with ROSE (Ranking of Super Enhancers), default parameters, H3K27ac BAM as signal and IgG as control, constituent enhancers = active enhancers overlapping ATAC peaks (no version)
Active-enhancer assessment: genome-wide 600 bp binarisation of H3K27ac signal over ChromHMM+ATAC active enhancers linked to >=1 target gene, followed by PCA across cell populations (no tool/version)

Definition of cell-type-specific and group-specific (Early B / Late B / B-cell) active enhancers by overlap rules (>=2 of 4 populations; >=5 B-cell types) and target-gene assignment from liCHi-C interactions (no tool/version)

TF motif set construction: HOCOMOCO v13 (HUMAN), primary (subtype 0) and quality A-C motifs, UniProt symbol standardisation with manual correction, expression filter (DESeq2-normalised median count >= 5 in >=1 cell type)
TF footprinting with TOBIAS (v0.17.0): ATACorrect bias correction, ScoreBigwig footprint scores, BINDetect binding calls, run per cell type on ATAC BAM + peak sets

Enrichment of TF binding in cell-type-specific enhancers and in primed regulatory loops: linear model of specific vs non-specific binding frequency, ranking by positive residuals, top 10 per cell type, expression cutoffs (median normalised >5; >=1 count for the loop analysis), HOCOMOCO v13 motif-similarity grouping (no tool/version)
Gene-centric 3D active-enhancer networks with R igraph (v2.1.4), degree centrality via degree(), heatmap with pheatmap (v1.0.13), custom radial plots with distance-normalised edges (1 unit = 500 kbp)

Gene expression ~ enhancer activity regulatory modelling: Additive / Synergistic / Redundant fits on DESeq2-normalised RNA and summed H3K27ac, BIC model selection with dBIC threshold 6 and sign rules, exclusion of genes with enhancers in <=2 cell types (no tool/version/fitting procedure named)
Bootstrap significance of primed regulatory DNA loops: 2,000 iterations sampling non-overexpressed control genes, empirical p = (#>obs + 1)/(n + 1) (no tool/version, no seed)

IHEC EpiAtlas retrieval: per-chromosome ChromHMM emission matrices from the standardized ChromHMM matrix directory + IHEC Metadata Harmonization File (v1.3); lymphoid-cancer filtering excluding T-cell samples -> 158 B-cell malignancy samples (18 B-ALL, 3 BL, 6 DLBCL, 3 FL, 5 MCL, 119 CLL, 4 MM)

IHEC enhancer bin map and activity scoring: 200 bp bins per B-cell stage / enhancer category, ChromHMM state extraction, enhancer states defined as 3-4 and 7-11, sample-level and enhancer-level enhancer activity scores, gene activity score from states 1-11 (no tool/version)

Genome-wide enhancer-deletion impact analysis on dbGaP WGS/RNA-seq (2,373 participants: MP2PRT phs001965.v1.p1, MMRF-COMMPASS phs000748.v7.p4, TCGA-DLBC phs000178.v11.p8, CGCI-HTMCP-DLBCL phs000235.v21.p6): Manta SV calls (upstream, unversioned), hypermutation filter >1,715 SVs, enhancer intersection, Affected/Unaffected stratification, Wilcoxon on VST counts, BH FDR

ERG / VPREB1 intragenic enhancer deletion analysis on 1,988 B-ALL patients via St. Jude Cloud: log2 CN ratio < -0.43 selection (ERG n=12, VPREB1 n=39), 20 permuted control sets, DESeq2 (v1.48.2) differential expression, Fisher combination with poolr (v1.2.0), 1.5 linear fold-change cutoff

Survival analysis on MP2PRT RNA-seq (n=1,479): DESeq2 normalisation, PCA on VST counts, CCND2 expression quartile stratification, Kaplan-Meier overall survival with log-rank test, univariate Cox HR Q4 vs Q1 (no package versions for survival/Cox; DESeq2 version not restated here)

GO Biological Process / Reactome / MSigDB pathway enrichment via Enrichr on selected gene sets (FDR < 0.05; background = all protein-coding genes, or expressed >5 FPKM; no background specified for the 3D-primed machinery analysis); manual grouping of GO terms into functional categories (no tool versions, no database release dates)

Epigenome browser gene-landscape figures via an 'in-house script' based on the Gviz R package: promoter interactions + CHiCAGO outputs, equal per-omic scale limits across cell types, smoothed BigWig tracks, collapsed transcript models (no version, no smoothing parameters)

headline.static_readiness: 0/35 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: 17/35 (49%) computational steps reach RI at the stage-1 prose ceiling. The 17 RI steps are those where every axis is >=1 and a named tool carries an exact version pin in prose (bowtie2 2.3.2, sambamba 0.7.0, samtools 1.9, deepTools 3.2.1, ChromTime v1.0.0, MACS3 v3.0.2, Trim Galore 0.6.6, STAR 2.7.0f, subread 2.0.2, HiCUP 0.8.2, CHiCAGO 1.14.0, ChromHMM v1.24, HOCOMOCO v13, TOBIAS v0.17.0, igraph 2.1.4, pheatmap 1.0.13, DESeq2 1.48.2, poolr 1.2.0). The other 18 steps cap at NI because the tool is unnamed, unversioned, or an explicitly in-house / custom script (QC metrics, consensus peak merging, disjoin segmentation integration, enhancer specificity rules, TF-enrichment linear model, BIC regulatory modelling, bootstrap, IHEC bin map, survival analysis, Enrichr/GO enrichment, Gviz browser script), and for ROSE, HiCaptuRe, Gviz and Manta which are named but unversioned. No step can exceed version=1 at stage 1: the paper and README claim no lockfile, conda environment, or container, so version pins are floating with respect to environment closure. Data axis is additionally capped at 1 for every step consuming study-generated or dbGaP/St. Jude data: EGA raw data is controlled-access via a Data Access Committee, the GEO SuperSeries GSE320196 is verified private until 2027-02-17, and the paper text itself states both accessions as '(pending)'.
headline.coverage: 35 computational steps assessed from Methods prose plus the GitHub landing page and README prose; 7 wet-lab steps counted (W) and marked X as out of computational-reproduction scope. Full text obtained from the bioRxiv .full HTML page (JATS XML endpoint returned HTTP 403). Repo read limited to README prose and top-level directory listing; no workflow source inspected.

gaps.where: Software environment for the entire pipeline (all 35 C-steps)
gaps.missing: No conda environment file, lockfile, requirements file, container image or digest, renv snapshot, or sessionInfo is claimed anywhere in the paper or in the repository README. Exact version pins exist in prose for roughly half the named tools, but with no environment closure; R itself, Bioconductor release, and OS/toolchain are never stated even though a large share of the analysis is R-based (CHiCAGO, HiCaptuRe, igraph, pheatmap, DESeq2, poolr, Gviz).
gaps.how_to_close: Ship a conda/renv lockfile or a container image with a pinned digest covering both the command-line tools and the R/Bioconductor stack, and record R sessionInfo alongside the analysis scripts.

gaps.where: Downstream analysis code (C14-C16, C19-C22, C25, C27, C28, C30, C31, C33-C35)
gaps.missing: The repository landing page (https://github.com/JavierreLab/B-Cell_Roadmap) exposes only README.md, LICENSE, a Preprocessing/ directory, and Data/Complementary_Data. The README states the repo 'contains the necessary data and scripts to reproduce the main analysis', but no directory corresponding to the downstream analyses (chromatin-state relabelling, enhancer specificity definition, regulatory BIC modelling, bootstrap, IHEC scoring, SV/deletion analysis, survival, enrichment, Gviz figures) is visible at the top level. Several of these are described in prose as 'in-house script' with no version, seed, or thresholds.
gaps.how_to_close: Add the downstream analysis scripts/notebooks to the repository, organised per figure or per Methods subsection, with the in-house QC, specificity, modelling and plotting code included.

gaps.where: Data availability - study-generated raw and processed data
gaps.missing: The paper states 'The data that support this study are available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request', and both accessions are given as '(pending)': EGA raw data and the GEO processed-data SuperSeries. The README supplies concrete identifiers (EGAS50000001612 / EGAD50000002310-2313 and GSE320196 / GSE320102-320105) but adds 'Data will be released upon manuscript acceptance'. Direct check on 2026-07-27 confirms GSE320196 is private and scheduled for release on 2027-02-17. EGA access is controlled and restricted to not-for-profit organisations subject to a Data Access Committee decision.
gaps.how_to_close: Release the GEO SuperSeries at preprint time (or provide a reviewer token in the manuscript) and replace the 'available upon reasonable request' clause with the concrete EGA/GEO accessions already listed in the README.

gaps.missing: dbGaP accessions are version-pinned (phs001965.v1.p1, phs000748.v7.p4, phs000178.v11.p8, phs000235.v21.p6), which is good practice, but access is controlled and requires an approved dbGaP request; the St. Jude Cloud PAX5-driven B-ALL collection (n=1,988) is likewise access-controlled and no dataset version/freeze date is given. The Manta SV calls are consumed as provided by the projects, with no Manta version recorded.
gaps.how_to_close: State the dbGaP/St. Jude data freeze dates actually downloaded and the Manta version associated with the consumed SV call sets, and provide derived, non-identifying intermediate tables (e.g. per-gene deletion carrier counts) so the statistical steps can be re-run without controlled access.

gaps.where: Reference genome and annotation (C2, C6, C10, C12, C18)
gaps.missing: The reference genome build is given as GRCh38.p13, but the source of the FASTA (ENCODE/GENCODE/Ensembl/UCSC flavour) is not stated, and the gene annotation GTF used by STAR and featureCounts is never identified by release. The restriction-enzyme target sequence used for the HiCUP in-silico digest is not given, nor is the liCHi-C capture design/bait file.
gaps.how_to_close: Name the exact genome FASTA and annotation release (e.g. GENCODE vNN) with download URLs, and deposit the liCHi-C bait/design file and digest configuration in the repository.

gaps.where: External databases and web services (C23, C29, C34)
gaps.missing: HOCOMOCO is pinned to v13 and the IHEC metadata harmonisation file to v1.3, but the IHEC EpiAtlas ChromHMM matrix release/download date is not stated, and the GO, Reactome, MSigDB and Enrichr releases used for enrichment are entirely undated. Enrichr is a live web service whose backing libraries change over time.
gaps.how_to_close: Record the access date and release version for every external database (GO, Reactome, MSigDB, Enrichr library, IHEC EpiAtlas freeze) and, where possible, ship the downloaded gene-set files with the analysis code.

gaps.where: Stochastic steps without recorded seeds (C18, C28, C32)
gaps.missing: ChromHMM LearnModel initialisation, the 2,000-iteration bootstrap of primed regulatory loops, and the '20 random permutations' of non-deleted control patients in the ERG/VPREB1 analysis are all stochastic, and no random seed is reported for any of them. The k-means clustering of promoter interactions (C14) also has no seed and no stated k.
gaps.how_to_close: Report random seeds (or ship the scripts with seeds set) for the ChromHMM model training, bootstrap, permutation sampling, and k-means clustering, and state the chosen k for the interaction clustering.

gaps.where: Parameter reporting by external reference (C9, C10, C1, C6)
gaps.missing: RNA-seq and CUT&RUN/ATAC processing are described as following 'ENCODE standards' with 'parameters recommended by ENCODE' and 'slight modifications'; the STAR flags are paraphrased rather than listed, the CUT&RUN trimming tool is not named at all, and the ATAC 'offset correction of the paired read' is described without a tool or shift value.
gaps.how_to_close: List the actual command lines (or ship the pipeline configuration) rather than pointing at an external standard, and name the trimming tool and the ATAC offset implementation.

gaps.missing: NRF / PBC1 / PBC2 and fingerprint AUC are computed, and libraries 'failing to meet the expected thresholds ... were flagged for potential exclusion or interpreted with caution', but the numeric thresholds are never given and the actual exclusion decisions are not recorded. Which libraries were dropped, and on which metric, cannot be reconstructed.
gaps.how_to_close: Publish the QC metric table per library with the applied thresholds and an explicit pass/fail/excluded column.

gaps.missing: The 15 ChromHMM emission states are relabelled into biological categories using 'prior biological knowledge'; TF gene symbols are 'manually corrected where necessary'; GO terms are 'manually grouped into functional categories'. None of these manual mappings is provided as a table, so they cannot be reproduced from the description.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the state-to-label mapping table, the TF symbol correction list, and the GO-term-to-category assignment as supplementary files or repository data.

gaps.missing: No workflow manager (Snakemake/Nextflow/WDL/CWL/make) is claimed anywhere, and no driver script or execution order is described beyond the narrative sequence of Methods subsections. The dependency graph linking primary processing to the 20+ downstream analyses is implicit.
gaps.how_to_close: Provide a workflow definition or at minimum a top-level driver script documenting the execution order and inputs/outputs of each stage.

gaps.where: Software identity / provenance of custom code
gaps.missing: The repository has no release tag, DOI (Zenodo/Software Heritage), or commit reference cited in the paper - only a bare GitHub URL. There is therefore no immutable pointer to the code state corresponding to this manuscript.
gaps.how_to_close: Archive the repository at a tagged release with a Zenodo DOI and cite that DOI in the Code Availability statement.

gaps.where: Intermediate result artifacts (enhancer catalog, interaction calls, chromatin state segmentations)
gaps.missing: The central derived resources of the paper - the specific active enhancer catalog, enhancer-gene assignment table, CHiCAGO high-confidence interaction sets, and ChromHMM segmentation files - are referenced throughout the analyses but their availability is bound to the embargoed GEO SuperSeries. Only 'Data/Complementary_Data' appears in the repository, whose contents were not inspected at stage 1.
gaps.how_to_close: Release the enhancer catalog, enhancer-gene links, interaction calls, and segmentation BED files as unrestricted supplementary artifacts independent of the GEO embargo, since they are derived summaries rather than individual-level data.
